title: Solo dev + AI workflow: 20 patches in one month for my browser tower defense
author: MasterSteak4510
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev,

I've been developing PCB Defense (a tower defense set on a circuit board) solo, using AI agents for most of the code iteration. Just shipped v3.7.0. Wanted to share what worked, what didn't, and get feedback on both the workflow and the game.

**The workflow:**

I structured it as a "design constitution" first — an ART_BIBLE.md and a CONSTITUTION.md that defined:
- Color tiers (T0 gray → T6 magenta) for every system
- Text style rules (no "player", no generic English, `// SYSTEM MESSAGE` format)
- Shape language (circle = pickup, triangle = enemy, hexagon = boss)
- Motion timing standards (0.15s micro, 0.4s medium, 0.8s dramatic)
- Banned patterns (emoji, marketing speak, "unlock powerful upgrades")

Every AI prompt I wrote referenced these docs. This prevented the agents from drifting into generic-sounding text or inconsistent visuals.

**What worked:**
- Agent-per-patch workflow with a recon → plan → implement → test cycle
- Every patch backed by a `.bak` file and tested with `node --check`
- Recent patches used headless Chrome CDP for behavioral tests (pixel diffing, state checks)
- Using AI for the "boring" parts (null guards, refactoring, culling) freed me for design

**What didn't:**
- Agents over-engineer when unconstrained. I had to explicitly tell them "don't add extra features"
- Test scripts kept breaking as line numbers shifted — needed semantic tests, not line-based
- Agents sometimes hallucinate game state. Required actual browser tests, not just code review
- Compounding debuff balance was a mess — agent balanced them in isolation, they stacked into run-enders

**The result:**
v3.7.0 has:
- 7 hidden cross-branch synergies (undocumented in game)
- 3 boss archetypes that decide which card pool you draw from
- Dynamic music with 8 intensity layers (level + boss + HP + combo + enemies)
- 15 event-triggered tutorial tips
- Full art bible + design constitution

Play: https://juba13.itch.io/pcb-defense

**Questions for this sub:**
1. How do you prevent agent context drift over many patches? I had good luck with the constitution doc, but I'm wondering if there's a better pattern.
2. Do you use agents for design decisions, or only implementation? I've been keeping design human-only.
3. Any pitfalls with long-running projects where agents gradually degrade quality?

Happy to share the constitution doc if anyone's interested.

replies.author: MasterSteak4510
replies.body: Actually, saying that only the appearance of the towers has changed would be an understatement. I’ve improved or replaced a great many visuals—some to make things look more pleasing, some to make it easier to distinguish the ground from the enemies, and others to dial up the chaos.
